title: Workspace
summary: A documented architecture for a future authenticated environment where assessments, evidence, recommendations, approvals, projects, generated reports, and governed AI workflows could become operational work. No public or provisioned workspace access is demonstrated by this page.
audience: Clients, partners, researchers, reviewers, learners, and operators using Aloha AI systems.
implementationStatus: Architecture and selected platform foundations are under development. No public sign-in, account creation, provisioned client workspace, or production access is represented as available.
roadmap: Connect public resource IDs to authenticated actions
Add saved learning and assessment progress
licensing: Workspace access is provided through defined engagements, pilots, programs, or licensed implementations.
methodology: Carry public resource context into the workspace
assumptions: Sensitive work is configured for the relevant access and retention requirements
limitations: Feature availability varies by engagement and maturity
Workspace output does not replace accountable professional judgment

blocks.text: The intended authenticated workspace would begin with an organization and a first project. Public sign-in, account creation, and workspace provisioning are not available from this page.

items: Overview: see the organization, active project, and current workspace state.
Drafts: persist work in progress against the correct organization and project.
Evidence: save titled source material and keep it attached to the work it supports.
Review: inspect the intermediate work, preserve approval behavior, and keep accountable judgment in the loop.

blocks.text: A draft belongs to an organization and project rather than an ungoverned chat. Evidence is stored with its title and source text so the workspace can keep claims, supporting material, and review together.
The public resource registry describes what each system does. The authenticated workspace carries that context into operational work, where access, persistence, review, and approval matter.

Workspace access is provided through defined engagements, pilots, programs, or licensed implementations. Feature availability varies by engagement and maturity, and workspace output does not replace accountable professional judgment.
